ZATCA (Saudi Arabia): Value Added Tax Law and Implementing Regulations — 5% from 1 January 2018, 15% from 1 July 2020
ZATCA guideline on professional services under VAT provisions: mandatory registration threshold SAR 375,000 (Implementing Regulations art. 5)
ZATCA: Implementing Regulations for Zakat Collection — art. 15 (zakat year is the fiscal year, twelve lunar months by default; day-count rule for Gregorian years)
mearef: Saudi Arabia — VAT rate (ZATCA VAT Law: 15% from 1 July 2020) and registration threshold (GCC Common VAT Agreement art. 50(2))

caveats: Non-Gregorian tax year (grade P, Implementing Regulations for Zakat Collection, art. 15, on zatca.gov.sa): a zakat payer's fiscal year is twelve lunar (Hijri) months - about 354 days, drifting roughly 11 days earlier each Gregorian year - and payers may adopt the Gregorian calendar year instead. The stored start (1 Muharram, approximated as 1 January) follows the default lunar year; Saudi and GCC nationals pay zakat (2.5% of the zakat base for a Hijri year; about 2.5778% by day-count for a 365-day Gregorian year), not income tax.
companyYearEndDefault is a 31 December app default (grade S): most Saudi zakat and tax payers keep a Gregorian year ending 31 December, and ZATCA assesses non-Hijri years by day count.
Effective dating of VAT (grade P, ZATCA's VAT Law and Implementing Regulations): VAT was introduced on 1 January 2018 at 5% and raised to 15% from 1 July 2020.
Registration threshold of SAR 375,000 taxable supplies over 12 months (voluntary at SAR 187,500; grade P, ZATCA's professional-services guideline citing art. 5 of the Implementing Regulations).
Returns are monthly where annual supplies exceed SAR 40,000,000 and quarterly otherwise (grade S); left as a caveat rather than a single frequency.
